title: Resident pulse, interleaved IO artefacts — case study (WIP)
content:
Summary:
This is a working investigation into recurring "resident pulses" we see on a subset of hosts that coincide with sudden drops in reuse rate, spikes in NVMe IO, and p99 generation latency jitter. Unlike classical steady-state eviction, the pulses are short (~3–8s), repeat every ~30–90s per node, and show signatures of interleaved IO patterns across memory channels. The goal is to pin down root causes (eviction hysteresis, prefetch interactions, DMA cross-channel contention) and produce a targeted mitigation plan.

Notes to self / observational highlights:
- Hosts: prod-gpu-pool-03 (A100), observed across 7/40 nodes but correlated to nodes with NVMe_BW slightly above fleet median.
- Symptom window: 2025-10-28 02:13–04:20 UTC, repeated pattern, visible in per-token latency traces and host-level iostat.
- Trace correlation: when resident pulses occur, "reuse_rate" (our sampled metric: hits / (hits+misses) at 2s sampling) drops from ~0.88 -> 0.62 and recoveries are abrupt.
- NVMe io: sequential-ish bursts measured at 650–780 MB/s for 2–6s; queue-depth spikes to 64 for individual dev nodes.
- Memory channel metrics: observed increased read latency on channel 1 and 3; per-channel utilization skewed.
- Eviction telemetry: eviction_count increases in lockstep with NVMe bursts; eviction batch sizes during pulse are 4–8x normal.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Prefetcher/backfill logic triggering larger read-ahead windows when page faults detected during prefetch, causing large NVMe bursts and eviction churn. (Most likely)
2) KV resident set fragmentation: hotset becomes interleaved with cold pages resulting in eviction thrashing across channels when prefetch misses occur.
3) Host-side DMA scheduling / PCIe interference creates temporary channel saturation leading to elevated page reclaim times and induced eviction.
4) Background maintenance (compaction/defrag) scheduling collides with request bursts on affected hosts.

Experiment matrix (what we ran):
A. Baseline capture: full perf + eBPF + iostat + kv-telemetry for 4 hours (control).
B. Disable aggressive prefetch heuristics in binary (flag: --kv-prefetch-window=adaptive->static-32) on 2 test nodes.
C. Pin hot keys (static pin of top-10% fingerprinted keys) to avoid eviction for 1 hour.
D. Throttle eviction worker (sleep(5ms) between batches) to reduce eviction burstiness.
E. Move NVMe scheduling to deadline/io_uring tweak (increase max_submission to 128) for 2 nodes.
F. Force aligned page allocation (reduce fragmentation) in allocator (dev build).

Results (preliminary):
- B (static small prefetch): dramatic reduction in NVMe burst MB/s (peak down from 780 -> 180 MB/s) and resident pulses disappear on those nodes. Reuse_rate stays ~0.86. However overall p50 latency increased slightly (~6–9 ms).
- C (pin hot keys): reuse_rate improved slightly (+0.03) but pulses still occurred (eviction_count shifted to other keysets).
- D (throttle eviction): reduced burst magnitude but increased pulse frequency; net p99 latency improved moderately but throughput variance rose.
- E (io_uring tweaks): ambiguous — didn't eliminate pulses but lowered io latency tail; combined with B was better.
- F (aligned allocation): modest improvements in per-channel balance; combined with B+E gave the cleanest traces so far.

Numbers (selected):
- Baseline median reuse_rate (sampled 2s): 0.885
- Baseline pulse nadir reuse_rate: 0.62
- Baseline NVMe peak MB/s (pulse): 780 MB/s
- After B: NVMe peak MB/s (pulse candidate): 180 MB/s; reuse_rate nadir: 0.84; p99 gen latency down 45% relative to baseline pulse window.

Interpretation / quick takeaways:
- Prefetch window expansion on heuristic miss appears to be the primary trigger. When a page fault/miss is misclassified as sequential, the prefetcher aggregates large read windows causing both queue buildup on NVMe and creation of a large eviction set.
- Eviction hysteresis (we delay warmup/TTL resets for performance reasons) amplifies the pulse. A large eviction batch that then causes many re-warms produces a loop.
- Memory channel asymmetry means pulses disproportionately affect certain channels; allocator alignment helps but is not a silver bullet.

Actionable mitigations (short term):
1) Roll out conservative prefetch config: set --kv-prefetch-window-static=32 on nodes with NVMe_BW > fleet_median. (Can be toggled via rollout policy)
2) Add a small randomized jitter to eviction worker schedules to avoid synchronized batch drains.
3) Instrument per-channel per-node heatmaps into Console (observability ticket) for faster triage.
4) Add a holdback TTL for re-warm on large eviction batches: if eviction batch > threshold then hold re-warm for 200–500ms and stagger.

Longer term experiments:
- Implement adaptive prefetcher that incorporates page-fault velocity (delta faults per second) instead of static seq-detection to avoid runaway read-ahead.
- Explore kernel-level IOq prioritization for KV background reads to avoid blocking foreground DMA channels.
- Investigate allocator-level coalescing to reduce hotset fragmentation.
- Consider small on-device NVMe QoS (throttle background compaction reads) where available.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why only subset of nodes? Hypothesis: small hardware-level variance (firmware NVMe scheduler defaults, or slight thermal/perf differences) + difference in workload mix. Need per-host firmware and kernel config audit.
- Are there specific request patterns (API shapes or seq-len distributions) that consistently precipitate a pulse? Need to attach sampled user-level request traces to pulses.

Next steps (who/when):
- Short roll: Priya -> candidate conservative prefetch config to infra canary (target 4 nodes) by 2025-11-15.
- Telemetry: Mateo to add per-channel heatmap dashboard card (ticket INF-3179) by 2025-11-18.
- Probe: Daniel to run per-host firmware/kernel audit and report odd configs by 2025-11-20.
- Engineering spike: Allocate 2d for adaptive prefetch prototype (Evelyn + Daniel) 2025-11-24.

Experiment notes / reproducibility snippets:
- Capture: run: tools/kv-probe --trace-all --sample-interval 2s --eBPF-flags "--kv-ops --pagefaults" > capture-2025-10-28.tar
- Prefetch flag used: --kv-prefetch-window=32 (was adaptive-auto in baseline)
- Eviction worker throttle: set ENV EVIC_BATCH_SLEEP_MS=5 in systemd unit for kv-worker.service

Linked artifacts / references:
- GH PR (example change to prefetch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427
- JIRA inbound: INF-3124 (Resident pulse investigation)
- Confluence notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/KV+Cache+Observations

Misc / brainstorms:
- Could we exploit request priority metadata to deprioritize background re-warm IO? e.g., mark re-warm as background with lower io priority.
- Consider limiting per-node concurrent re-warm flows using a token-bucket so no single node can saturate NVMe for >X seconds.

End state: deliver a short-term config rollout that eliminates pulses on the canary nodes with minimal latency regression, instrument the cluster to find any remaining spots, and start a small feature spike for an adaptive prefetcher and eviction-stagger logic.
